manifest.name: @local/dsh-edge-search
manifest.description: 让 Harness 通过 CDP 驱动本机 Edge 浏览器：网页搜索、读正文（内置 web 工具被 SSRF 防护拦住时的兜底通道）
manifest.author: Chuzhj

meta.title: Edge 浏览器兜底
meta.description: 通过 CDP 驱动本机 Edge 做网页搜索、读正文。无需任何 API Key，也不受 web_fetch 在 VPN fake-ip 模式下的拦截影响。

readme.text:
简体中文 | [English](README.en.md)

一个 **DeepSeek Harness**（DSH）的 Host 插件，通过 CDP 驱动
**你本机真实的 Edge 浏览器**，给 agent 补上 `edge_search` / `edge_read` 两个工具。
不要 API Key，不接第三方服务，不花一分钱。

它的主业是**给内置 web 工具兜底**——尤其是你在开 VPN 的时候。

<!-- 截图：把图片放到 docs/screenshot.png 之后，取消下面这行注释，效果远比纯文字强

-->

---

DSH 自带的 `web_fetch` 有一层 SSRF 防护：域名解析一次，**只要解析出的地址里有一个不是
公网单播，整批结果直接拒绝**，连请求都不发。

而 Clash / Mihomo 系 VPN 的 **fake-ip 模式**（默认池 `198.18.0.0/15`，RFC 2544 保留段）
会把**每一个**域名都解析成 `198.18.x.x`。两边一撞，`web_fetch` 在**所有站点**上都报：

```
URL hostname "..." resolves to a non-public IP address
```

这不是某个网站的问题，也不是你网络坏了——`curl`、浏览器、`Invoke-WebRequest` 都好好的，
只是 `web_fetch` 在发包之前就把自己拦住了。

本插件绕开这层检查：浏览器自己解析域名、自己开 socket，系统把流量送进 VPN 隧道，
插件只负责把渲染好的页面读回来。

> 十秒自测（Windows）：`Resolve-DnsName www.baidu.com`。返回 `198.18.x.x` 就说明 fake-ip
> 开着，`web_fetch` 对所有域名都废了。

---

| 工具 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `edge_search` | 后台标签页打开搜索结果页，提取 `标题 / URL / 摘要`，然后关掉标签页。引擎支持 `bing`（默认）/ `baidu` / `google` / `duckduckgo` |
| `edge_read` | 后台标签页打开指定 URL，用文本密度策略提取正文（站点改版也不怕），然后关掉标签页 |

两个工具都**只返回纯文本、无状态**，不会碰你已打开的标签页，也**不需要登录**。

它们是**兜底通道，不是默认通道**：比 `web_fetch` 慢一个数量级，只在内置工具失败或你
不想花按次计费的搜索费时才用。

---

- 装好 DSH（桌面版或 CLI 都行）
- **Windows** + **Microsoft Edge**。用别的 Chromium 内核浏览器可以通过 `edgePath` 指定
- 运行时**没有 npm 依赖**，也不需要任何 Key
- 想在 DSH 之外跑离线自测，需要 **Node.js 22 或更高**：插件用到了全局 `WebSocket`，
  Node 20 及以下会报 `WebSocket is not defined`（DSH 自带运行时不需要你操心）

---
有两种方式。**新手直接用方式一 —— 一条命令都不用敲。**

readme.section: 方式一：把整个文件夹交给 DSH，让它自己装（最方便）
readme.text:
不用开终端、不用手改 JSON，让 DSH 的 agent 自己动手。

1. **把 `dsh-edge-search` 整个文件夹拖进 DSH 对话框**（或者直接把完整路径发给它）。
   注意是**整个文件夹**，不是其中某个文件 —— 它要能看到 `package.json` 和 `index.js`。

2. **附上一句话**（直接复制）：

> 帮我安装这个 DSH Host 插件：先把它复制到 `D:\tools\dsh-edge-search`
   > （固定位置，不要放临时目录），再登记到 profile 的 `dependencies` 和
   > `dsh.profile.bundles` 里，包名是 `@local/dsh-edge-search`。
   > 顺便把仓库里的 `skills/web-fallback` 整个文件夹复制到 `%DSH_HOME%\skills\` 下
   > （这是一个配套技能，装上它 agent 才更容易想起用这两个工具）。
   > 装完告诉我需要重启。

readme.section: 方式一：把整个文件夹交给 DSH，让它自己装（最方便）
readme.text:
3. DSH 会自己执行 `dsh plugin --profile desktop add`、把包名写进 bundles 配置，
   并把配套技能复制到 `%DSH_HOME%\skills\`。

4. **最后由你手动完全退出 DSH，再重新打开。**
   Host 插件只在启动时加载，而这一步它自己做不到 —— 它没法重启自己。
   少了这一步，工具不会出现，看起来像「装失败了」。

装完验证一下：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop list
```

出现 `@local/dsh-edge-search@file:...` 就成了。也可以在对话里让它随便读个网页试试。

> 如果 agent 说自己没有终端权限、或者报 `dsh: command not found`，退回方式二手敲。

---

readme.section: 1. 把插件放到一个固定位置
readme.text:
clone 或解压到一个你以后不会挪的目录，比如 `D:\tools\dsh-edge-search`。
目录根下必须有 `package.json` 和 `index.js`。
```powershell

readme.section: 用 CLI 的话，把 desktop 换成你自己的 profile 名
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile desktop add D:\tools\dsh-edge-search
```

这一步把它登记成 `file:` 依赖并安装到 profile 里。

> 包名 `@local/dsh-edge-search` 里的 `@local` 是刻意的：**它不发布到 npm**，
> 只从本地路径安装。`package.json` 里的 `"private": true` 也是同一目的——防止误发。

readme.section: 3. 注册成 bundle —— **这步别跳过**

readme.text: Host 插件在启动时加载，必须**完全退出再打开**，不是刷新窗口。

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop list
```

应该能看到 `@local/dsh-edge-search@file:<你的路径>`。

然后在 DSH 对话里让 agent 读个网页，它手里就该有 `edge_read` 了。也可以不经过 DSH，
直接跑离线自测：

```powershell
node selftest.mjs probe                              # 只看调试端口通不通
node selftest.mjs read "https://example.com" 400
node selftest.mjs search "你好" bing 3
node selftest.mjs js "https://example.com" "document.title"   # 在页面里跑任意 JS，探查用

> **第一次调用时会弹出一个 Edge 窗口。** 那是插件的专用调试实例（独立 profile，
> 不含你的书签、密码、Cookie），**不是你的日常浏览器窗口**。让它开着——关掉的话
> 下次调用会重新拉起，多花 5–10 秒。

---

写在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里：

```yaml
- id: dsh-edge-search
  name: "@local/dsh-edge-search"
  config:
    port: 9222

| 键 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `port` | `9222` | CDP 端口，必须没被占用 |
| `edgePath` | 自动探测 | `msedge.exe` 的路径。Edge 装在非标准位置时填；指向的文件不存在会直接报错，不会静默回退到自动探测 |
| `profileDir` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-edge-search\edge-profile` | 自动化专用的独立浏览器 profile，闲置时随便删 |

---

readme.section: 原理 / 一条必须知道的硬约束
readme.text:
```mermaid flowchart LR A["agent 调用 edge_read"] --> B["插件"] B --> C["启动 / 复用
独立 profile 的 Edge"] C --> D["新建后台标签页"] 关键在于：**DNS 解析和 socket 都在浏览器里完成**，不经过 DSH 那层 IP 校验。 这就是它能绕过 fake-ip 拦截的全部原因。 Chromium 136 起，浏览器用**默认数据目录**时会**静默忽略** `--remote-debugging-port`。 所以本插件永远带一个专用的 `--user-data-dir` 启动 Edge，而不是去接管你日常那个窗口。 别想着"优化"掉这个参数——去掉之后调试端口根本不会监听，而且**没有任何报错**。 每次调用都是新建一个后台标签页、干完活、关掉。你自己的窗口一律不碰。 ---

- **CDP 端口只监听 `127.0.0.1`**，不接受外部连接。但**本机上的任何进程**都能连上它——
  在共享电脑或不可信环境里需要留意。不用时直接关掉那个 Edge 窗口即可。
- **调试 profile 是独立的**，位于 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-edge-search\edge-profile`，
  不含你的书签、密码、Cookie 和登录态。这也是「读不到需要登录的页面」的原因——
  是设计，不是缺陷。
- 插件**不向任何第三方服务发送数据**，没有遥测、没有统计上报、没有 API Key。
  所有请求都是你的浏览器直接发往目标站点。

---

| 现象 | 原因 | 处理 |
|---|---|---|
| `unknown tool "edge_read"` | 插件没加载 | 用方式一装的，先确认有没有**手动重启** DSH；还是不行就检查方式二的第 3 步（`bundles`） |
| `配置项 edgePath 指向的可执行文件不存在` | 路径写错 | 检查路径，或删掉该项让插件自动探测 |
| `Edge did not expose a debugger on port 9222` | 端口被占，或找不到 Edge | `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 9222`；改 `port` / `edgePath` |
| 第一次调用要 5–10 秒 | 正在拉起 Edge | 正常。调试窗口别关，后续调用会复用它 |
| `extracted no readable text` | 纯 JS 应用 / 登录墙 / 空页面 | 不是 bug，确实没正文可提 |
| 要登录才看得到的内容 | 专用 profile 里没有你的 cookie | 设计如此，这种内容请用你自己的浏览器 |

耗时参考：`edge_read` 约 2–10 秒，`edge_search` 约 3 秒，首次调用额外多 3–8 秒。

---

**更新到新版本**：

```powershell
cd D:\tools\dsh-edge-search
git pull

readme.section: 然后完全退出并重启 DSH
readme.text:
```

**关掉那个调试用的 Edge 窗口**：直接关窗口就行，插件下次调用会自动重新拉起。

**想彻底重置**（比如 profile 被搞乱了、端口状态不对）：powershell
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\dsh-edge-search\edge-profile"
```

---

readme.section: 手工安装（`dsh plugin add` 用不了时）
readme.text:
直接改 `%DSH_HOME%\profiles\<profile>\package.json`，**两处都要加**——依赖和 bundle：

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@local/dsh-edge-search": "file:D:/tools/dsh-edge-search"
  },

然后让 profile 重新解析依赖，再重启 DSH：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop install
```

⚠️ 只改 `dependencies` 不跑 install，pnpm 的 lockfile 会继续指向旧路径。这时候插件加载会失败，
而且**通常没有任何报错**，只表现为"工具不存在"。

---

1. 从 profile 清单的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里删掉 `"@local/dsh-edge-search"`
2. `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove @local/dsh-edge-search`
3. 重启 DSH

---

readme.section: 配套技能（可选，但强烈建议装）
readme.text:
`skills/web-fallback/SKILL.md` 是给 agent 看的判断规则：**什么时候**该换用这两个工具。

**不装也能用**——插件装了，工具就在。但 agent 未必会在 `web_fetch` 失败时想起去试
`edge_read`；装上这份技能，它遇到 `WEB_BLOCKED_URL` / `resolves to a non-public IP
address` 时会主动切过来。

readme.section: 装法一：让 DSH 自己装
readme.text:
用「方式一」装插件时，那句指令里已经带了这一步（`skills/web-fallback` 复制到
`%DSH_HOME%\skills\`）。如果你已经装完了插件、只补技能，直接说：

> 把 `dsh-edge-search\skills\web-fallback` 整个文件夹复制到 `%DSH_HOME%\skills\` 下。

`%DSH_HOME%` 一般是 `C:\Users\<你的用户名>\.dsh`。技能放在它下面的 `skills\` 里，
**一个技能一个文件夹，文件夹里必须有 `SKILL.md`**：

```powershell

readme.section: 把 D:\tools\dsh-edge-search 换成你实际放插件的位置
readme.text:
$src = "D:\tools\dsh-edge-search\skills\web-fallback"
$dst = "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\skills\web-fallback"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dst | Out-Null
Copy-Item "$src\SKILL.md" $dst -Force
```

装完的目录结构应该是这样：

```
C:\Users\<你的用户名>\.dsh\skills\
└── web-fallback\
    └── SKILL.md
```

然后**开一个新会话**（技能在会话启动时加载，老会话看不到），问一句
「你现在有哪些技能？」，能看到 `web-fallback` 就成了。

如果你以前装过同功能、但**名字不同**的技能（比如 `web-fetch-fallback`），
**先删掉旧的再装这份**。两者的触发条件几乎完全一样，同时存在会互相抢，
行为变得难以预测。

```powershell
Get-ChildItem "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\skills" -Directory | Select-Object Name

readme.section: 确认是旧的再删（下面只是举例，按实际名字改）
readme.text:
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\skills\web-fetch-fallback"
```

直接删文件夹即可：

```powershell
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\skills\web-fallback"
```

---

见 [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)。从 v0.3.0 起开始记录。

English | [简体中文](README.md)

A **DeepSeek Harness** (DSH) host plugin that gives the agent two extra web tools —
`edge_search` and `edge_read` — by driving **your real Microsoft Edge** over the Chrome
DevTools Protocol. No search API key, no external service, no billing.

Its main job is being the **fallback when the built-in web tools stop working**, which happens
to everyone running a VPN in fake-ip mode.

<!-- Screenshot: drop an image at docs/screenshot.png and uncomment the line below.

-->

DSH's built-in `web_fetch` has an SSRF guard: it resolves the hostname once and **rejects the
whole answer set if any resolved address is not public unicast** — before sending a single byte.

Clash / Mihomo style VPNs in **fake-ip** mode (default pool `198.18.0.0/15`, an RFC 2544
reserved range) answer *every* DNS query with a fake address like `198.18.0.107`. The two
designs collide and `web_fetch` fails on **every site** with:

```
URL hostname "..." resolves to a non-public IP address
```

This is not site-specific. Your network is fine — `curl`, browsers and `Invoke-WebRequest` all
work — but `web_fetch` refuses before it ever dials out.

This plugin sidesteps the check entirely: the browser resolves the name and opens the socket,
the OS routes the traffic into the VPN tunnel. The plugin only reads the rendered page back.

> Quick self-check: `Resolve-DnsName www.baidu.com` on Windows. If it returns `198.18.x.x`,
> fake-ip is on and `web_fetch` is dead for every domain.

---

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `edge_search` | Opens a search-engine results page in a background tab, extracts `title / url / snippet`, closes the tab. Engines: `bing` (default), `baidu`, `google`, `duckduckgo`. |
| `edge_read` | Opens a URL in a background tab, extracts the main readable text with a text-density heuristic (survives most redesigns), closes the tab. |

Both are **text-only and stateless**, never touch your existing tabs, and require **no login**.

They are a **fallback channel, not the default one**: an order of magnitude slower than
`web_fetch`. Reach for them only when the built-in tool fails, or when you want to avoid a
billed search API call.

---

- DSH installed (the app or the CLI — either works).
- **Windows** with **Microsoft Edge**. (Another Chromium browser can be forced with `edgePath`.)
- **No npm dependency at runtime**, and no API key.
- To run the offline self-test outside DSH you need **Node.js 22 or newer** — the plugin uses the
  global `WebSocket`, so Node 20 and below fail with `WebSocket is not defined`.
  (DSH ships its own runtime, so this only matters for the standalone self-test.)

---
There are two ways. **If you are new to this, use option 1 — no commands to type.**

readme.section: Option 1: Hand the whole folder to DSH (easiest)
readme.text:
No terminal, no hand-editing JSON — let the DSH agent do it.

1. **Drag the entire `dsh-edge-search` folder into a DSH chat** (or send it the full path).
   It must be the **whole folder**, not a single file — the agent needs to see `package.json`
   and `index.js`.

2. **Add this instruction** (copy as-is):

readme.section: Option 1: Hand the whole folder to DSH (easiest)
readme.text:
> Install this DSH host plugin for me: first copy it to `D:\tools\dsh-edge-search`
   > (a permanent location, not a temp directory), then register it in the profile's
   > `dependencies` and `dsh.profile.bundles`, package name `@local/dsh-edge-search`.
   > Also copy the `skills/web-fallback` folder into `%DSH_HOME%\skills\` — it is a companion
   > skill that helps you remember to reach for these tools.
   > Tell me when I need to restart.

readme.section: Option 1: Hand the whole folder to DSH (easiest)
readme.text:
3. DSH runs `dsh plugin --profile desktop add`, adds the package name to the bundles config,
   and copies the companion skill into `%DSH_HOME%\skills\`.

4. **Quit DSH completely and relaunch it yourself.**
   Host plugins are only loaded at startup, and the agent cannot restart itself.
   Skip this and the tools simply will not appear — it looks like the install failed.

Verify:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop list
```

readme.section: Option 1: Hand the whole folder to DSH (easiest)
readme.text:
`@local/dsh-edge-search@file:...` should be listed. You can also just ask the agent to read a
page in the chat.

> If the agent says it has no terminal access, or reports `dsh: command not found`, fall back
> to option 2 and type the commands yourself.

---

Clone or unzip it to a folder you will not move, e.g. `D:\tools\dsh-edge-search`.
The folder must contain `package.json` and `index.js` at its root.

readme.section: 2. Add it to your DSH profile
readme.text: ```powershell

readme.section: replace "desktop" with your profile name if you use the CLI
readme.text:
dsh plugin --profile desktop add D:\tools\dsh-edge-search
```

This registers it as a `file:` dependency and installs it into the profile.

> The `@local` part of the package name is deliberate: **this is not published to npm**, it is
> installed from a local path only. `"private": true` in `package.json` enforces the same thing.

readme.section: 3. Register it as a bundle — **don't skip this**

readme.text: Host plugins are loaded at startup. Quit the app completely and launch it again.

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop list
```

should show `@local/dsh-edge-search@file:<your path>`.

Then, in a DSH chat, ask the agent to read a page. If it has the tools, `edge_read` appears in
its tool set. You can also run the offline self-test without DSH:

```powershell
node selftest.mjs probe                              # is the debug port up?
node selftest.mjs read "https://example.com" 400
node selftest.mjs search "hello world" bing 3
node selftest.mjs js "https://example.com" "document.title"   # run arbitrary JS in the page

> **The first call pops open an Edge window.** That is the plugin's dedicated debug instance
> (separate profile — no bookmarks, passwords or cookies of yours), **not your everyday browser
> window**. Leave it open: closing it just means the next call relaunches it and takes 5–10 s.

---

Config lives in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, under the `dsh-edge-search` entry:

```yaml
- id: dsh-edge-search
  name: "@local/dsh-edge-search"
  config:
    port: 9222

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `port` | `9222` | CDP port. Must be free. |
| `edgePath` | auto-detected | Path to `msedge.exe`. Set it if Edge is installed somewhere unusual. A path that does not exist raises an explicit error instead of silently falling back to auto-detection. |
| `profileDir` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-edge-search\edge-profile` | A separate browser profile used only for automation. Safe to delete when idle. |

---

readme.section: How it works (and the one constraint that matters)
readme.text:
```mermaid flowchart LR A["agent calls edge_read"] --> B["plugin"] B --> C["launch / reuse Edge
with a dedicated profile"] C --> D["create a background tab"] The important part: **DNS resolution and the socket both happen inside the browser**, so the request never passes through DSH's IP check. That is the entire reason this plugin works.

readme.section: How it works (and the one constraint that matters)
readme.text:
Chromium 136+ **silently ignores** `--remote-debugging-port` when the browser uses its default
data directory. That is why this plugin always launches Edge with a dedicated
`--user-data-dir` instead of trying to attach to your everyday Edge window. Do not "optimise"
that away — remote debugging will simply stop listening with no error.

Each call creates a background tab, does its work, closes the tab. Your own windows are never
touched.

---

- **The CDP port binds to `127.0.0.1` only** and does not accept external connections. However,
  **any process on the same machine can connect to it** — worth keeping in mind on a shared or
  untrusted computer. Close the Edge window when you are done.
- **The debug profile is isolated**, at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-edge-search\edge-profile`. It holds
  none of your bookmarks, passwords, cookies or sessions. That is also why login-walled pages
  cannot be read — by design, not a bug.
- The plugin **sends no data to any third-party service**. No telemetry, no analytics, no API key.
  Every request goes straight from your browser to the target site.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `unknown tool "edge_read"` | Plugin not loaded | Installed via option 1? Make sure you **restarted DSH manually**. Otherwise check option 2, step 3 (`bundles`) |
| `edgePath` points at a file that does not exist | Typo in the path | Fix it, or remove the key to fall back to auto-detection |
| `Edge did not expose a debugger on port 9222` | Port taken, or Edge missing | `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 9222`; set `port` / `edgePath` |
| First call takes 5–10 s | It is launching Edge | Normal. Keep the debug window open; later calls reuse it |
| `extracted no readable text` | JS-only app, login wall, or empty page | Not a bug — nothing to extract |
| Content behind a login | Dedicated profile has no cookies | By design; use your own browser for that |

Expected latency: `edge_read` ≈ 2–10 s, `edge_search` ≈ 3 s, plus 3–8 s on the very first call.

---

**Update:**

```powershell
cd D:\tools\dsh-edge-search
git pull

```

**Close the debugging Edge window**: just close it. The plugin relaunches it on the next call.

**Full reset** (e.g. the profile got into a weird state):powershell
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\dsh-edge-search\edge-profile"
```

readme.section: Manual install (if `dsh plugin add` is unavailable)
readme.text:
Edit `%DSH_HOME%\profiles\<profile>\package.json` by hand, adding **both** entries — the
dependency *and* the bundle:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@local/dsh-edge-search": "file:D:/tools/dsh-edge-search"
  },

Then let the profile resolve it, and restart DSH:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop install
```

readme.section: Manual install (if `dsh plugin add` is unavailable)
readme.text:
⚠️ Editing `dependencies` without running install leaves pnpm's lockfile pointing at the old
path. The plugin then fails to load, usually with no visible error — only a missing tool.

---

1. Remove `"@local/dsh-edge-search"` from `dsh.profile.bundles` in the profile manifest.
2. `dsh plugin --profile desktop remove @local/dsh-edge-search`
3. Restart DSH.

---

`skills/web-fallback/SKILL.md` is a DSH skill that tells the agent **when** to reach for these
tools.

**The plugin works without it** — install the plugin and the tools are there. But the agent may
not think to try `edge_read` when `web_fetch` fails. With this skill installed, it switches over
on its own when it hits `WEB_BLOCKED_URL` / `resolves to a non-public IP address`.

The instruction in "Option 1" above already includes this step. If you already installed the
plugin and only want the skill, just say:

> Copy the `dsh-edge-search\skills\web-fallback` folder into `%DSH_HOME%\skills\`.

`%DSH_HOME%` is usually `C:\Users\<you>\.dsh`. Skills live under its `skills\` folder —
**one folder per skill, and each folder must contain `SKILL.md`**:

```powershell

readme.section: replace D:\tools\dsh-edge-search with wherever you put the plugin
readme.text:
$src = "D:\tools\dsh-edge-search\skills\web-fallback"
$dst = "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\skills\web-fallback"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dst | Out-Null
Copy-Item "$src\SKILL.md" $dst -Force
```

The layout should look like this:

```
C:\Users\<you>\.dsh\skills\
└── web-fallback\
    └── SKILL.md
```

Then **start a new session** (skills are loaded at session start), and ask "what skills do you
have?" — `web-fallback` should be listed.

If you previously installed a skill with the same purpose but a **different name** (e.g.
`web-fetch-fallback`), **remove the old one first**. Their trigger conditions overlap almost
completely, and having both makes the agent's choice unpredictable.

```powershell
Get-ChildItem "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\skills" -Directory | Select-Object Name

readme.section: delete the old one once you are sure (name is just an example)
readme.text:
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\skills\web-fetch-fallback"
```

Just delete the folder:

```powershell
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\skills\web-fallback"
```
